newsitem.title: CHINA: China schools to halt college exam exemptions.
newsitem.headline: China schools to halt college exam exemptions.

text.p: China has suspended a system exempting some high school students from taking college entrance exams to prevent abuse by children of the rich and powerful, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

Education authorities were halting until 1998 a practice whereby high schools could recommend their top students for exemption from gruelling college entrance exams, the newspaper quoted Zhou Liming, an official with the ministerial-level State Education Commission, as saying.
Officials would draw up guidelines aimed at stopping schools from making recommendations based on money or connections rather than academic ability, Zhou said.
"Some schools were pressured into recommending students not worthy of exemption because their relatives were government officials or provided financial support to the schools," Zhou said.
China's national college entrance exams are extremely competitive, with just a tiny fraction of one percent of the population receiving a university education.
